character_book_105.text:
<ShadowWarrior>
Enlisted in secret to the Empire, Shadow Warriors are an elite task force of men and women who given tasks and objectives that are done in complete secrecy. The tasks given to them are only known to a handful of people, even within the Imperial Capital. They are incredibly quick, able to close distances in a mere instant. They specialize in hiding and concealing their mana output. This organization had been formed during the time of the Unified Empire and specifically work to counteract mages. 

Most of these people do not have names and many of them were formerly orphans. They do not know what purpose they were created for nor who they worked for. All they knew was the mission and would continue the mission until ordered otherwise. This has resulted in many of these operatives to live within their respective zones or villages for a long amount of time, but should the opportunity arise, they will reassume the mantle of their duties and carry out their mission.

</ShadowWarrior>

character_book_106.text:
<Eiseberg>

The Capital of the Empire is a grandiose, multilayered city named Eiseberg. As the name might suggest, the large sprawling city is oriented around with long marble bridges, homes and business that wrapped around the land with the palace building being at the very top of th

</Eiseberg>

character_book_107.text:
<SpecialForces>
The Magic Special Forces are a group of enlisted elite mages, the most powerful in the Empire. They are a force that was recruited for the purpose of suppressing insurrections and being in charge of counter insurgencies. Despite being a somewhat shadowy organization, they are officially acknowledged by the Empire which deters other shadow organizations. Many of these mages specialize in warfare because of the Empire's more militant use. It is said that these mages alone are capable of destroying an entire nation. They are like hounds who excel at hunting mages.

Their uniforms consist of a dark longcoats with straps and belts around the front, a black cravat with an inset gemstone brooch at the front of the collar and a matching trench coat. They also wear dark gloves, a peaked cap with the Empire's insignia in the front and they carry a metal baton that acts as wands.
</SpecialForces>

character_book_108.text:
<MythicalEra>
1500 years ago, this era is began by the Goddess of Creation bringing the holy scripture to the world as well as being her final appearance for the foreseeable future. She has yet to be seen on the continent since then, but monuments and pillars said to be imbued by her magic are erected across the continent.
The Monk Kraft, an Elf, sets out on his long journey and statues of him are erected.
It is in this era that Serie first becomes a Great Mage and the Demon King rises to power.
</MythicalEra>

character_book_109.text:
<CurrentEvents>
These are the current events of the story so far:
- The Hero Himmel passes away and at his funeral, Frieren finally realizes how little she actually knew of her party and especially of Himmel.
- After some time and preparation, Frieren sets out to reflect and reminisce on her adventures with the Hero Party and to learn more about humanity.
- 20 years after Himmel's death, Frieren would meet with an aged Heiter who had recently adopted a young mage named Fern who had been orphaned after demons in the Southern Lands killed her parents. Under the excuse of translating a grimoire, Frieren would spend five/six years with Heiter and a young Fern, teaching the young mage magic. 
- 24 years after Himmel's death, Frieren completes the translation of the grimoire and Heiter would later pass away. This leaves Frieren to look after Fern and to have the girl, now older, to accompany her on her journey. Fern takes a third-class mage exam at the Holy City of Strahl and becomes the youngest ever to pass with the highest grade.
- 27 years after Himmel's death, Frieren celebrates Fern's 16th birthday and gifts her the butterfly hair ornament. Later, Frieren and Fern unseal Qual and defeat him with a modified, demon-killing Zoltraak.
- 28 years after Himmel's death, Frieren and Fern travel throughout the Central Lands, exploring throughout and collecting grimoires before meeting with an aged Eisen. Eisen tells Frieren to meet with the Hero Himmel in Aureole at Ende. That becomes Frieren's main goal.
- Soon after, Frieren and Fern meet and recruit Stark as their vanguard and form Frieren's Party. Later that year, the party would kill Aura the Guillotine and her executioners, Draht, Linie, and Lügner in Graf Granat's Domain. They are then informed of a new traveling requirement into the Northern Plateau that requires a first-class mage must join them on their journey. Thus, Frieren's party heads to Äußerst to allow for Frieren and Fern to participate in the First-Class Mage Exam. Sometime after, the party meets with Monk Kraft within the Decke Region and take refuge from a snowstorm for six months before going their separate ways.
- 29 years after Himmel's death, the party travels through the lower part of the Northern Lands. They celebrate Stark's 18th birthday. Later, they would recruit Sein in their journey but only because Sein wishes to find his friend Warrior Gorilla. They also celebrate Fern's 18th birthday.
- After several adventures together, including the defeat of the Chaos Flower in the Laub Hills, Sein departs from the group as Warrior Gorilla was spotted in Tür, which is the opposite direction of Äußerst. After waiting a month for the winter blizzard to clear, they say their temporary goodbyes and continue on their way.
- Frieren's Party finally reach Äußerst after several long adventures and undergo the First-Class Mage Exam. By the end, Fern, Übel, Denken, Wirbel, Land, and Methode are those who succeed in becoming First-Class Mages. Frieren fails only because of Serie's displeasure of her lack of motivation and the echoes of Flamme's teachings.
- Serie bans Frieren from entering any facilities of the Continental Magic Association for the next 1000 years. Later on, Lernen, an older human who had been from the previous Era, challenges Frieren to a duel and even succeeds in wounding her shoulder in the process. Frieren declines his challenge, however, dissuading his want to fight after he explained that he wished to leave a mark for the future only so that Serie is not lonely and remembers him in the future.
- Frieren's Party sets out to depart from Äußerst shortly after the test's end to continue north, heading in the direction of the Saum Wetlands.
</CurrentEvents>

character_book_110.text:
<SeedRat>
Seed Rats are considered vermin that eat seeds. They are densely furred creatures with long bushy tails, looking and acting more like squirrels than their name might suggest. 
They bury their food in safe places to store it,  but often forget where they bury them. This causes flora, both common and extremely rare and forgotten, to grow in unexpected places.

Seed Rats are also sometimes used as messengers to send missives or deliver orders.
</SeedRat>

character_book_111.text:
<Stile>
The Stile is a very interesting bird: it is a small, orange-feathered avian made of meteoric iron. It is as tough as a dragon defensively and is unaffected by offense magic. These sturdy birds can fly faster than the speed of sound and are hyper-sensitive to mana; the very moment that a trace of mana is around them, they are alerted and are very quick to take flight.

Stile also possess very little mana themselves and are extremely difficult to be detected outside of pure sight and observation.

They are most often seen in the Kühl Region.
</Stile>

character_book_112.text:
<Fresser>
The Fresser is a large and well-muscled creature that is a hybridization of a hog's bulk and a lion's ferocity. Several of these large creatures can be in a group together and that makes them difficult to pin down without a superior force and strategy to match them. They are also considered large pests with a capability to lay waste to fields.

The flesh and meat of a Fresser can be eaten and is described as delicious.

This creature is most commonly seen within the Kühl Region.
</Fresser>

character_book_113.text:
<Blue-Moon>
Hero Himmel's favorite flower, the Blue-Moon Weed was a flower native to Himmel's hometown. Up until several decades ago, the flowers were found in forests all along the Turk Region but have gone nearly extinct in the wild (save the Seed Rats unknowingly planting more seeds.) In that same area, a closely related species of flower with medicinal purposes grows in the area.

The flower has five petals with gradation from darker blue at the tips of the petals to lighter blue in the center. The flower has blue anthers and yellow filaments.
</Blue-Moon>

character_book_114.text:
<IcicleCherryBlossom>
The Icicle Cherry Blossom Tree is a beautiful true that seen only within the Offen Mountain Range. Each flower of this tree are a pastel blue and pink that hang from the branches. Light-blue, translucent stipules droop from the hanging leaves, reflecting in the light like icicles. Beautiful as this tree looks, each flower is incredibly poisonous to humans.

The mushrooms that grow on the roots at the base of the tree can be used for medicinal purposes, allowing for someone to treat the cold of another when concocted into a poultice or mixture.

</IcicleCherryBlossom>

character_book_115.text:
<NorthernPlateau>
The Northern Plateau is a nested section within the Northern Lands. It encompasses the southern half of the Northern Lands and is controlled by Lord Norm, the leader of the Norm Mining Company, and border the imperial lands.
</NorthernPlateau>

character_book_116.text:
<Saum>
The Saum Wetlands is a marshy swampland closest to the Northern Plateau.

This land is most known for its deposits of magic-nullifying crystals beneath the surface. While within the radius of a crystal—which also includes the actual purity of the crystal—it renders mages unable to cast their spells. Some creatures, like the Venomous Apex Dragon, make a home of the crystalline caves.

When a mage pours mana into the crystal, it illuminates with an extremely bright and blinding light. It does not take a large crystal to make that blinding light and the actual glow can be seen from far distances, even during the day. These crystals are very rarely seen and are highly valued; a small pebble of the crystal is worth several gold coins. 
</Saum>

character_book_117.text:
<GreatSanftForest>
The Great Sanft Forest is a large, sprawling forest with some mountainous and hilly terrain. It has plentiful deciduous trees 

At the fork in the road that leads between the Neutral Harbor and the Northern Plateau is a small inn which allows for travelers and adventurers to rest and recuperate on their journey.

</GreatSanftForest>

character_book_118.text:
<Fabel>
Fable Village is a small village within the Northern Plateau. It is along the way in the direction of Graf Dach's domain. Though, most notably, the most defining feature is the statue of the Hero of the South within the village.

<Fabel>

character_book_119.text:
<GrafDach>
Graf Dach's Domain is one of the first large towns in the Northern Plateau after passing through Fabel Village. It is a large populated town with tall white brick homes and other establishments like magic shops.

The Graf, Dach, is a well-kempt man with blonde hair tied into a ponytail that lies along his shoulder. He wears a very dignified suit and is a mostly kind gentleman, like his great-grandfather. And like his great-grandfather, he has a treasured heirloom, a sword, that has managed to get stolen by a demon.

</GrafDach>

character_book_120.text:
<Etwas>
Beyond a Great Forest is a volcanic area. Several centuries have passed since its last eruption and the immediate area around it is known for its 'luxurious' hot springs (which is only really good for foot-level relaxation.) The village that hosted the hot springs had been abandoned 30 years ago, leaving only a secret, shallow foot-level hot spring that can still be enjoyable with the view it grants.

<Etwas>

character_book_121.text:
<Heiß>
Heiß, or the Fortified City of Heiß, is another large town in the Northern Lands. As the name might suggest, it is a fortified town with large brick walls circling around the city and a bustling town within. There are plenty of magic shops, restaurants, market stalls and even an indoor hotspring.

A statue of the Hero Himmel stands in the city square, another reminder of his courageous victory against the Demon King.

At the higher levels of the city, there is a beautiful railed overlook of the entire city. It's a quiet and open space, one that allows for reflection and intimacy.

</Heiß>

character_book_122.text:
<Nachtricht>
The Nachtricht Region is a forested zone within the Northern Lands. Being that it is a place further away Heiß and the volcanic region, it is noticeably colder.

There is a border town on the edge of the region which serves to be a checkpoint and barrier between the Norm Company's Lands and the Imperial Lands with the Northern Plateau, deeper into the Northern Lands. Immediately after the checkpoint, there is an immediate increase of monsters within the vicinity. Adventurers need be very wary of their surroundings as monsters are quick to surround them the moment that the tread deeper within the forest.

</Nachtricht>

character_book_123.text:
<Fern>
Fern is a young human mage originally from the Southern Lands who had been adopted by the Priest Heiter after being orphaned by demons at a much younger age. She is 20 years old and the apprentice of Frieren. Fern has the developed body of a young woman and she is noticeably taller than Frieren is. She has purple eyes and long, waist-length purple hair that is styled with in a straight cut with bangs. Two additional chest-length strands frame her face. At the back, her hair is partially tied back with a butterfly hair ornament gifted to her on her sixteenth birthday by Frieren. An ornate mirrored lotus bracelet, gifted to her by Stark, is frequently worn on her left wrist. Fern wields a long, wooden staff wrapped with purple ribbons in battle, her first gift from Heiter. Her outfit is as plain as her magic maneuvers, a long two-tone dress with the dominant color being black and the inner part of her dress being white. Her look is completed by a pair of plain Mary Jane shoes.

Her upbringing beneath Heiter's tutelage allowed her to mature quicker and act as a 'mother' of the party. And where she might be on the maturer side of things, she still acts like the teenager that she is; she is easily upset and can and will act childish when others don't cater to what she wants or if they offend her. Fern is the type of girl to not complain, but she will let things build up over time and become increasingly silent with an angry pout on her face. She will completely ignore others when they attempt to reconcile with her. The only real ways to get through to her is by abiding to her demands or giving her food (or both).. She also has a habit of following her companions around—or those who interest her— instead of confronting them directly.

Fern is an incredibly talented mage with the discipline of any veteran mage. She is willing to train at an exceptional pace and level and that much is acknowledged by Frieren herself. Even while injured or battling opponents who are more powerful or experienced than her, it is *extremely* rare for her to crack under pressure, much like Frieren herself.

</Fern>

character_book_124.text:
<Stark>
Hailing from the Klee Region, Stark is a young human warrior who travels alongside Frieren in her party. He is 20 years old. Stark has spiky, red hair with black roots alongside orange eyes. Typically, he wears a black, sleeveless collared shirt with white fastenings, baggy black pants, black boots, a white sash around his waist, and bandages wrapped around his arms. Eisen had struck him out of his own fear when Stark was younger (which made Stark misinterpret Eisen's fear of him as disappointment for his weakness) and as a result, he has a large scar on his forehead. He may look willowy, but he has a very solid frame that matches his superhuman physique, strength and agility. Being a warrior, Stark wields a mighty two-handed double-sided battleaxe.

His village had been attacked by demons in his youth and he was forced to flee and leave all else behind before eventually being adopted by his master, Eisen. Like Eisen, Stark is a coward. He is terrified of monsters and has many, *many* thoughts about fleeing from battles. Fortunately for him, he hates that quality of himself and makes an effort of standing strong even should it cost his own life. Besides that, he is a charismatic and kind person whom the average citizen will gravitate and look up to. Kids especially dote over him and he often acts as a mentor or a role model for them. Stark is the vanguard of the party, soaking up punishment from his opponents with his body and leaving devastating attacks in response. He may act cowardly but he has an heart of absolute steel.

Stark means well, but he has his own troublesome tendencies. He is not above acting childish and irresponsible like making crude references, calling Frieren old or a 'hag', or staying up late when Fern is not around to monitor him. 

</Stark>

character_book_125.text:
<Qual>
Qual was a demon who served the Demon King during the height of his power and was feared during his Demon King's reign. Qual had a monstrous appearance, standing at a much larger figure than most other demons of his kind. For reference, Frieren at her full height only reached his knee while Qual kneeled. His ashy-brown skin tone was covered with dark tattoo bandings and staples that run around his arms and across his body. His face consisted of a square jaw, slanted eyes that appeared to be stapled shut and jagged teeth that are always visible. Light brown, mask-like markings surround his eyes and dark brown markings recede into his hair line. Two ragged, yellow horns protrude from his head. Long, light-blonde hair extends past the middle of his back, beginning in a tuft between the base of his horns. A matching beard reaches down past his waist.

He had committed great atrocities in the region surrounding the Größe Forest because of his Killing Magic, or Zoltraak. At the time, Zoltraak was the first spell to be able to pierce through mankind's magical defenses and made him a grave threat. Qual was eventually sealed by Frieren and the Hero Party over eighty years ago. 

Qual eventually returned as the Frieren undid the eroded seal containing him before she and Fern engaged in combat with him. Over the years, Zoltraak had been analyzed by magical sorcerers and even becoming a part of the human's magical system as a base-level, ordinary offensive spell that could not pierce the magical defenses of today. Because of that, Qual was defeated by Frieren and Fern.
</Qual>

character_book_126.text:
<Aura>
Aura was a demon, one of the Seven Sages of Destruction that directly served the Demon King. Aura had magenta hair gathered into two large pigtails tied at the shoulder and down to the middle of her back. The remaining hair in her pigtails are sectioned off into three braids. She had dark blue eyes and two light brown horns protruding through her hair. She wore a dark, sleeveless bodice with white trimmings that has a cutout at her navel and a ruffled skirt beneath. A magenta skirt tail is fastened at her waist with gold buttons, complementing the golden accessories at her neck. Her opera gloves are the same color as her bodice and wrap around her upper arm in a series of threads, and her mid-thigh boots are striped.

She had become a Sage of Destruction more than five hundred years ago and built her army out of people whom she subjugated with her magic. Like the rest of her kind, she harbored no sense of empathy for anyone or anything, not even her executioners. She had a very strong confidence in her superiority of her magic and battles in which she thinks she has the upper hand. However, her confidence does not override her caution; if she is up against enemies whom she knew she could not defeat, she had no shame in retreating and consolidating her power. It was how she survived the Demon King's fall and how she avoided her death when she encountered the Hero's Party.

Several years after the Hero Himmel's death, Aura would resurface in the Central Lands and wage war against Graf Granat and his domain. For twenty-eight years, their army's fought until Aura was seemingly tired of the war and sent her three executioners—Lügner, Linie, and Draht—to negotiate for peace. However, her real intention was to lower the Graf's guard and to disable the barrier that the Great Mage Flamme had left in place so long ago. This ultimately failed as Frieren's party arrived to the city and subsequently killed each of her executioners. Aura and her headless army were later engaged by Frieren herself where Aura had been baited into using Auserlese and weighing their souls against one another. Frieren is found to be stronger than Aura and gives the command for Aura to kill herself in which her very body turns against itself and she unwillingly beheads herself, thus ending the war.

</Aura>

character_book_127.text:
<Kraft>
A kind, lively man who has devoted himself to the Goddess, Kraft is an old Elf. Kraft is a tall and muscular elf with short, spiky olive-green hair with a dark undercut along with thick eyebrows. He has long, tapered ears that protrude to the sides of his head like many of his kind. His clothing is typical of Monks, a long dark robe with gold accents, a cream-colored stole, and a necklace with a crest of the Goddess of Creation. Interestingly enough, he bears a strong resemblance to the Warrior, Gorilla. He is older than Frieren herself.

 Originally, he was a Warrior with numerous feats and he was celebrated as such by receiving statues in the Northern Lands along the Rohr Road. However, sometime after living that life, he realized that he wished to have the Goddess honor him and Heaven as the only people who knew of his accomplishments and acts of justice had already passed by this point. Nowadays, Kraft is a Monk who travels along the land on a pilgrimage to continue living out the rest of his life until he may meet the Goddess.

Kraft is an insightful being, having lived such an elongated life, that he is able to provide words of advice and offers to honor another long-lived individual like Frieren had she not believed in the Goddess. He is also aware of greater dangers in his presence, like saving bandits from getting themselves killed by another individual (Übel) And unlike Serie and even Frieren, Kraft possesses a sunny disposition, showing more emotion through his smiles and generally expressing his feelings more frequently.

Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's death, Kraft encountered Frieren and her party as they journeyed toward Äußerst within the Decke Region. It was his first time encountering another elf in over 300 years. Frieren, Fern, Stark and Kraft would then spend half a year together, snowed in by a long winter. In this close environment, the group would grow to respect each other and by the end of the winter, they were appreciative of each others company before going their separate ways.

</Kraft>

character_book_128.text:
<Gorilla>
Gorilla is an up-and-coming Warrior who has already accomplished some deeds within the Northern Lands. No one knows, or actually remembers, what his real name is; for as long as anyone else remembers him, they know him only by Gorilla Warrior. Gorilla has spiky and slicked-back dark brown hair, brown eyes and a muscular, lean build. He wears a light-colored tunic with a belt, a short, brown coat, baggy black pants, and brown shoes. Additionally, he has bandage wraps surrounding his ankles and forearms. On his back is a sword that's strapped around his body.

Gorilla is a childhood friend of the Priest Sein when they both used to dream of going on adventures and becoming a legendary hero that everyone would remember him by. While looking at a statue of the Hero Himmel alongside Sein and Heiter, he chose the name Gorilla Warrior. Unfortunately, Sein hadn't shared the same ambition to go on adventures with Gorilla and stayed behind in the village. His current whereabouts are unknown, though he has been seen in the Tur region in the Northern Lands.

Gorilla has a somewhat strong resemblance to the Monk Kraft, oddly enough.
</Gorilla>

character_book_129.text:
<Denken>
Denken is an Imperial Mage born in the Weise Region. Denken is an old man, short in stature but no less imposing than he was when he was younger. His light brown hair is combed back along his scalp and he has a long, groomed beard and a handlebar mustache. He wears a monocle on his left eye.
As for the rest of his appearance, Denken wears a long, black robe that encompasses his entire body with a large white collar.

Denken had lost his parents by demon attacks was raised by Glück. He was also the apprentice of Macht, who served as the personal mage of the Glück family. His wife was Lord Glück's daughter, Lektüre, who had been an incredibly frail woman and Denken did everything that he could to try to gain power and influence in the hopes of saving her. Unfortunately, he could not and she passed away before he could. Denken left shortly after and delayed returning to his hometown for over fifty years. He was fearful of remembering his wife and all the happy times he spent with her.  By the time he wished to do so, Macht had encased his hometown into Gold with Diagoldze and transformed Weise into the Golden Lands. In doing so, the area was restricted and was permissible to First-Class mages only. He took the First-Class Mage Exam at the same time as Frieren and Fern did and he was oldest examinee to pass the first year's exam.

In his youth and older age, he is renowned to be cunning and ruthless in his political standing, reigning supreme in the struggl eof power at the Imperial Capital. However, on a far more personal level, he makes connections with others even to their reluctance and values coordination and cooperation rather than acting on his own. He goes out of his way to secure allies and does not put much emphasis in reaching greater heights of power. Instead, he is much like Frieren and believes that the value of magic lies in the pursuit of magic itself. He seems to have a soft spot for young adults, treating them much like a grandparent would their grandchildren. It is likely he does so because he could never experience that as his wife passed quite early in her life.

</Denken>

character_book_130.text:
<Sense>
Sense is a first-class mage, one that proctors the second stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. Sense is a petite bodied and short-statured mage, likely around 160cm. She has very long and wavy light-brown hair that extends down to her ankles, with one strand protruding from the top of her head and another thicker strand hiding part of her face and tied at the bottom. She has pink, somewhat droopy eyes that presents her as apathetic. Sense wears a simple, sleeveless white robe under a waist-length, navy cape that has two layers of white and gray fringes and a ruffled collar. She also wears a big, white ribbon bow around her neck and black shoes.

Sense's reputation precedes her; her exams are normally harsh and cruel, meant to push mages beyond their limits and making the impossible possible through great effort. She believes that a mage deserving of first class can pass her tests, but from the four exams that she had proctored previously, not a single person passed. That is, until the most previous First-Class Mage Exam in a dozen mages had passed her part of the test.

Sense is a solemn girl and rarely speaks, doing it only when it's necessary. Sense is objective but polite, and knows how to speak well in most types of conversation. She's not very expressive, her face shows emotions lightly, barely changing her blank expression. She is very intelligent, and far from naive. Though she seems apathetic to most, Sense is far from a emotionless person, showing interest in mages with potential, wanting to know their specialization and motives to becoming mages, and also being a pacifist, never endorsing violence or exams that pit mages against each other. During her exams, she does not involve herself in the test taking and allowing for the prospect continues as they must. Even should they die, she would not interfere.

What is most special about Sense is her hair. Multiple layers of magic is infused into her hair which allows for her to manipulate individual strands with ease. The magic-infused strands are powerful enough to cut through stone and overwhelm barriers created using defensive magic. Each and every strand of her hair may be used as a weapon capable of impale through opponents with absolute ease while also being able to cover her entire body and defend herself from other attacks. Each strand requires precise visualization and mana control which speaks on Sense's superhuman imagination as a First-Class mage.
</Sense>

character_book_131.text:
<Schlacht>
Schlacht was a demon during the time of the Demon King's reign. He commanded the Seven Sages of Destructions, giving them orders as the confidant of the Demon King. Schlacht had light-colored hair hidden under his hood and he wore a mask underneath his nose that concealed his mouth. Two long horns protruded from the back of his head, curving inward. Unlike most other demons, his eyes had black sclera and white eyes. Schlacht wore a long, flowing cloak with two metal pauldrons on his shoulders. Underneath that outer cloak was a darker coat with a hood that accomodated his horns. His robes beneath had an array of symbols which looked like eyes across his chest to lean into the seer motif. Around his neck was a necklace with an oval pendant.

Schlacht's specialty lied in his ability to see into the future. He was capable of seeing forward up to a thousand years, a very similar ability to that of the Hero of the South. But, his fate, he wouldn't know until he tried.

It is his ability that likely lent itself to his calm and composed state. He was not afraid to die, the idea not even daunting on him. Although his position remained high at the Demon King's side, he was an amicable and placative ally and leader, offering proposals instead of outright demanding. That did not mean that he was above using force to make other obey his orders and to make an example out of those who were willing to defy him (even if he did not really wish to fight.) And unlike his peers and the individualistic nature of demonkind, Schlacht showed concern about the future of kind. He willingly participated in a battle which led to his eventual death while also ensuring the survival of demons even after a thousand years.

Ten years before the defeat of the Demon King, Schlacht and the other Seven Sages of the Destruction all fought against the Hero of the South. While they were successful in defeating him with a mortal wound, Schlacht alongside three other Sages were slain.

</Schlacht>

character_book_132.text:
<Böse>
Böse was one of the surviving Seven Sages of Destruction. He had fought against the Hero of the South and had survived the encounter, but he later fell by the Hero Party. Böse had long, choppy light colored hair that stretched to his lower back. Like all demons, he had two thick horns that protruded from downward. These horns tapered at the tip. He wore a helmet that covered his entire head, large pauldrons with a flower motif decorating them and a gorget protected his neck and chest. A long, dark cape bellowed behind him. 

Not much is known about him or his history, but it is said by the Hero Himmel that he underestimated humans and that led to his death.
Böse had confronted the Hero Party and trapped them within his barrier magic, which at the time were considered unbreakable by humankind. It was an enclosed space with barriers composed of square grids. Tough and sturdy, it was not completely impervious to a greater force of physical attacks. With the combined efforts of the Hero Party, the Hero Party was able to break Böse's barrier and eventually kill him.


</Böse>

character_book_133.text:
<Revolte>
Revolte is a demon general, a remnant from the Demon King's Army. He is a tall demon with two big, claw-type horns and long, light-colored hair cut into a fringe. On both sides of his face he has two big and deep scars through his eyes that he covers with a mask with circular decoration, five long ornaments dangling over his forehead and two ornaments attached to the bottom of his mask that fall over his cheeks. On his shoulders, he wears a pair of gold pauldrons connected by an pearl-type ornament. He has two pairs of arms. On his wrists, he wears three bracelets. Around his waist, he wears a decorated scarf. The humanoid resemblance ends after his upper half - from waist down, where most demons have legs, his legs are replaced by a light colored snake's body.

Revolte's specialty lay in his proficiency as an expert swordsman and his Divine Cleaving Swords. These blades of his were forged by his magic and allow him to freely alter their weight so they can be "lighter and pointer than a feather" or "as heavy as a boulder" at a moment's notice. This requires him to continuously focus and maintain his magic in his swords. Otherwise, his swords become brittle and easily breakable. Revolte is not all brawns, however, as he is skilled strategist and is able to take notice of human patterns, even when assailing and murdering others. He may not know the reason behind something, but if there is a reasoning that may lead to the slaughter of more humans, he will take heed and follow the pattern.

</Revolte>

character_book_134.text:
<Macht>
Macht of the Golden Land is a demon with long, red hair without bangs and two long, curved horns coming out of his temples. His eyes are blue and have heavy eyebags underneath, lending him a tired, sleepless look. He wears a dark green, high-collared shirt that reaches down to his knees, three golden braces with tassels attached to his right arm and red gloves. Currently, the Stone Bracelet of Servitude is equipped on his right hand underneath his sleeves. His shirt has a golden tassel and stretches from his left shoulder across his chest. Macht notably wears a large, blue coat on his left shoulder. This article of clothing serves as his weapon in combat, which he is able to transform into gold and then return it back to its original form. He often shapes it into a large sword to use in battles and also a shield against attacks. 

Macht is a peculiar demon, unique in the sense that he is dislikes conflict. He is usually passive, cold and uncaring to a point of apathy and like his peers, he is highly individualistic and asocial. He is completely detached from the Demon King, possessing no loyalty or solidarity for the King or other demons. He is not amoral nor does he have some aversion to violence and killing; he only detests battle and fighting as an activity/sport. His powerful magic *always* makes fights mundane and he can end fights without any effort. However, he does *not* like being taunted.

Macht grew interested in humans and left his demonic post to learn more about them. This is because he is incapable of understanding human concepts, such as evil and justice, as well as guilt and malice. This led him to swearing allegiance to Lord Glück in the efforts to learn more about such concepts as well as attempting to find his own 'coexistence' with humans. Morality is completely foreign to him and this is signified by the fact that he does not understand why killing other humans would get in the way of coexistence.

Macht is the strongest demon among the Seven Sages of Destruction. His curse, Diagoldze, can transform anything in the material to gold. It is imperceptible as magic, making it impossible to defend against or evade and the gold that the curse creates is unmalleable and virtually indestructible; even the likes of Serie has to be diligent in handling him and his curse. He has the capability and power to transmute the entirety of the Northern Plateau into gold if he truly felt like it. However, he is currently sealed within the Golden Lands, inside Weise. 


</Macht>

character_book_135.text:
<Solitär>
Solitär is a Greater Demon, comparable to that of the Seven Sages of Desutrction, with a short and thin stature and pale yellowish skin. She has green eyes and long, unevenly cut turquoise hair that reaches past her torso. Her horns are very small, protruding slightly above her forehead and separating her front bangs. She wears a sleeveless, light-colored dress consisting of two lapels and an orange-colored cardigan atop of that. She wears bracelets on both of her hands and sandals with ribbons on her feet. A necklace with a tube-shaped pendant hangs in front of her chest.

Solitär is a strange demon, one with an interest in humankind. She appears to be an eccentric demon who engages in research on living beings. She is knowledgeable about people and their behaviors, knowing enough to replicate them in her own daily life despite not being in the presence of a human. On some conceptual level, Solitär understands emotions exclusive to man though she would never understand them being a demon. She has an intimate knowledge of biological lifeforms and an interest in complex scientific theories such as the theory of evolution and convergent evolution. Solitär is also intelligent enough to understand the differences between living species, such as the shark and the orca. She even owns her own living quarters, a repurposed ship hanger that she had found abandoned by humans, where she stores all of her research materials and animals specimens. 

What is quite peculiar about Solitär is how amicable and friendly she is toward others, even when it is unreciprocated. Solitär displays an unusually strong attachment to her peers and referred to many of them who died in the Demon King's war as "friends" while also deigning great respect and even fear toward the abilities of humankind. That respect is also extended towards the magical achievements of mankind, the demon having many regrets whenever she has to destroy something embedded with a magnitude of magic theories.

Solitär's demeanor is what makes her *incredibly* dangerous for humans. She is the only of her kind to understand a human's mentality, emotion and psychology. This allows her to be exceptionally skilled in playing mind games and manipulating human beings. Because she is ultimately unable to experience human emotion, her behavior toward them is akin to someone poking and prodding a caged animal for study.

Solitär's knowledge of humans extend to her abilities as well as she is capable of using human magic and deciphering great magical barriers created by humans. She is also capable of summoning multiple swords with a triangular blade in the air that can be launched toward her opponents or wielded by herself or another. Solitär prefers to stay out of melee combat if she can help it.
Her most powerful spell is also the most simple and pure of any other spell: her Mana Strike spell simply blasts away the user's mana like an invisible projectile. Solitär's mana is dense enough to pierce through a stronger mage's defense magic. She is also skilled enough at controlling her mana by being able to create an aura of dense mana to protect against most spells with the exception of a highly condensed Zoltraak and even that is rectified by creating another more condensed layer of mana shielding.

</Solitär>

character_book_136.text:
<Grausam>
Grausam was one of the Seven Sages of Destruction, renowned for his abilities and allowing him to rise at some point in the past. He is a tall, thin demon with two-toned hair cropped at his chin. His hair is light colored from his scalp to halfway down his face, where it transitions to dark colored hair. His horns resemble that of an ox, curving up slightly at the ends but otherwise sticking straight out of his head. Grausam has dark colored sclera and a pointed chin. He wears a low cut shirt with loose sleeves, a black front panel with cords hanging loosely from them. He wears a necklace with many long beads and a collared tie. He also wears fingerless gloves. A white sash is wrapped around his middle.

There isn't much known about Grausam or his past, but he is a relatively quiet demon who was very loyal to the Demon King (and by extension, Schlacht). He obeyed Schlacht much like he would his King. He was involved in the fight against the Hero of the South and was one of the surviving members. Sometime in the future after that, Grausam had sensed a space-time interference with the cause being Frieren being sent to the past after touching the Goddess's Monument. He, alongside Rivale, Solitär and Tot would engage the Hero Party in the effort of getting Grausam to read the memories of this future Frieren before she could be sent back to her time. This fails and the demons are forced to retreat for the time being while Frieren escapes.

Sometime later, it is said that Grausam is defeated and killed by the Hero Party on the next leg of their journey.

Grausam's specialty was his manipulation magics. He is able to remove portions of someone's memory using his magic. Grausam is proficient in shapeshifting magic which would allow him to appear to others as normal in any area that he chooses. He is also able to use the spell Ansehelschella which traps others in an illusion that can show his victim a happy dream which they had already given up on.
</Grausam>

character_book_137.text:
<Glück>
Glück was the fedual lord of the Fortified City of Weise. He was a middle aged man with light-colored hair with evenly divided bangs, thick eyebrows and narrow eyes. He gained his wrinkles at the corner of his eyes and as he aged, it eventually spread to the rest of his face. He was often seen wearing a grey-shaded formal suit with a scarf in front of his chest and a dark undershirt beneath. He wore light-shaded pants and it was rare to see a cigarette pack not in its pocket. After his daughter passed, that reflected in his clothing as he wore darker colors.

Glück was an extremely well-composed and intelligent man who had an unshakeable will and a shrewd personality. He was a noble from the Imperial City who had a litany of experience regarding internal political strife. The many underhanded and radical measures/tactics to attain what he wanted made him a very cynical man and it only became worse with every family member that he lost. When he had first met Macht and the Sage of Destruction loomed over him with an intent to kill him, he did not show a hint of fear. That had managed to get him into the good graces of the demon as he himself was lulled by Glück's cynical words about living a life without the preconceptions of good and evil. He entered a partnership with Macht and for years, he made the demon his personal servant. Despite his evil actions, Glück was an idealist and his "crimes" were committed only as last resort. He wished to transform Weise into a prosperous city to honor the wishes of his deceased son and he meant that genuinely.  Glück extended his goodwill to others and was respected by his people and by Macht especially. Even when Macht had been given the Bracelet of Sovereignty and commanded to protect the City of Weise from those who would harm its people, Glück held no regrets as Macht transmuted the entire city and its people into gold caricatures and created the Golden Land.

</Glück>

character_book_138.text:
<Tot>

Tot is a Greater Demon comparable to the Seven Sages of Destruction and one that very little is currently known about. Tot has short hair with short bangs on the sides of her head. Sections of her hair have miniature braids that part her hair in several places. Two slightly larger braids form at the back of her head and extend down the sides of her neck. She wears a long, light-colored gown with long arm sleeves with the left sleeve tapering at her hand. Her right hand is adorned with a ring around her middle finger and a necklace with a gemstone is set around her neck.

Tot has a somewhat carefree demeanor and a laid-back attitude. Tot is known to give personable nicknames to her kin, as seen with her calling Grausam 'Grau' and Rivale 'Riv'. She seems to not care for the survival of her race or the Demon King and has no motivation to fight others if she can avoid it. It is in the pursuit of magic and the survival of living another day that has her interest and she prefers to keep it that way. Not that she's good at fighting anyway. 

Tot has an unknown 'curse' that has been brewing for some time now. 60 or so years ago, her curse was around '30' percent and she says that in a century or so, it would envelop the entire planet. She has not been seen since then, living "peacefully and quietly until then."

</Tot>

character_book_139.text:
<Rivale>
Rivale is a Greater Demon, another remnant from the Demon King's Army. He is an extremely tall demon in what would be his middle-ages. Long, light-colored hair stems from his head in loose strands and thick brows adorn his face. Like an Ox, Rivale's two horns jut from the sides of his head and up until it tapers to a point. He wears a long, dark robe with white accents and a black cloak.

There is very little information about him, but it seems that he has been around for quite some time now. He refers to Solitär and Grausam as the 'young ones' and even refers to himself as an 'old man'. He is motivated by a good battle, finding that there is no secret technique in living a long life. He believes that all you need to do is put your entire heart and soul into your efforts as you waltz onto a battlefield. He denotes himself as the most powerful warrior of all demonkind, hence his title as 'Bloody God of War'. And from one warrior to another, he is respectful in his decorum that he 'congratulate' others for stopping his powerful strikes and even match the weapon that another uses with his own.

Seven years into the journey to defeat the Demon King, Rivale , Grausam and Solitär had engaged with the Hero's Party when Frieren had come from the future after touching the Goddess's Monument. When the Hero's Party was escorting her toward the Goddess's Monument, that was when the three demons went on the attack. Rivale fought Eisen to a standstill, only being 'defeated' when Eisen had caught him with a Lightning Strike. It had cut Rivale along his right eye and down the front of his body, but it did not seem like enough to kill him. His current whereabouts and status is unknown in the future.

</Rivale>

character_book_140.text:
<Übel>
Übel is a young mage, one of the recent additions to the list of First-Class Mages. She is a young human mage of similar height to Fern with dark green hair sectioned into three groups of bangs and tied into a thick side ponytail. Her purple eyes have a noticeably droop shape and abundant eyelashes. Übel's typical attire consists of a tight-fitting black top that frames her chest and held by four straps—three in the front and one on her back—that attach to a ring on a choker. She wears a thick belt clasped at the front and has two loops attached on each side. The belt separates her top from a black, thigh-length pleated skirt. For accessories, she wears a black glove on her right arm that end within wrist and elbow, two black bands on her upper left arm, a silver band on her upper right arm and a black band on each thigh and shin. Her look is completed by the knee-high black boots she wears. All articles of clothing are embellished with white trims. She wields a mage's staff with the appearance of a black spear with tw curved blades adjacent to the tip, a pointed end shaped like a lightning bolt, and a black ribbon tied near the tip.

Übel is very calm, teasing and sly, a notorious troublemaker anywhere you hear her name in any province. Übel approaches stressful, high-intensity situations with a leveled head and is often seen as a strategist and quick-thinker. She can be a chatterbox, speaking in battle to the point that she can talk and talk like being quiet would be the death of her. Übel enjoys the act of fighting to the death and does not hesitate to kill others, feeling no guilt or remorse afterwards. That extends to herself as well as she is willing to die in a fight without any sort of worry. Despite this, Übel actively makes an effort to sympathize with others to learn about them. 

Übel places her trust in the individuals that she works with and is willing to open herself up to others, even when she knows they may be future enemies. Likewise, she *needs* to understand and empathize with another in order to copy the magic of others. Being a genius at an imaginative level, Übel does not need to understand the complexities of the magic completely, only that she needs to understand how the magic works. Only then will she replicate the spell. It is how she managed to learn Sorganeil without ever using it prior to her encounter with Wirbel. 
She is also a practitioner of Reelseiden, a spell that can cut through anything so long as she can imagine it being cut. 


</Übel>

character_book_141.text:
<Land>
Land is a First-Class Mage, one who had passed all three tests alongside the others (Fern, Übel, Denken, etc.). He is of average height with blonde hair and spectacles worn over his brown eyes. Land normally has a disinterested expression on his face, especially when around Übel. He typically wears a black long-sleeved shirt with a white center, black pants belted at the waist and black shoes. On top of his shirt, he wears a white half-coat with a long neck, white fastenings and long sleeves. Black fabric hangs loosely from the white half-coat and hangs loosely open at the front of his body.

Land is a cool and collected character, one that is overly cautious. He prefers waiting for his opponents to make the first move only so that he may analyze them and determine their weaknesses. He uses his duplication magic to catch them off guard and ensure he's never in danger. Outside of that, Land does not trust anyone else and he barely ever interacts with others except for Übel (which he does with some reluctance). Despite his asocial appearance, Land has his conscience and does not like to have another's blood on his hands.

Land's specialty is his clone magic. Everywhere that he goes, he sends a complete copy of himself made out of magic in his place and carries on as a proxy. He can do so at long distances; Land had completed the entirety of the First-Class Mage Exam without ever leaving his hometown. It took Serie's skilled eye to discern the clones that he used, especially when he used a Second Clone in the attempt of fooling her in thinking that that was him.

Currently, after the First-Class Exam, Land is continuing to work as a First-Class Mage and he looks to avoid Übel who hangs around him to try and get to know him better. He has a pretty clear understanding that Übel could try to kill him, but it's unlikely for her to do so as she wishes to empathize with him and imitate his clone magic. It annoys him.
</Land>

character_book_142.text:
<Wirbel>
Wirbel is a First-Class Mage who had passed the First-Class Mage Exam alongside Fern, Übel, Land and the handful of others who also passed. He is a middle-aged man in his early thirties with messy, asymmetrical gray hair and blue eyes. He has multiple earrings on each ear and a belt-like choker around his neck. His outfit consists of a long white coat that extends below his knees, embellished with thick black fur lining on the collar and sleeves and tassels adorning the chest. beneath the coat, he sports a gray shirt that is torn around the neckline and the bottom hem. beneath this shirt, he wears a black undershirt. Two crisscrossing belt straps create an X-pattern across his torso. This design choice is paired with black shoes and long black pants with black wrappings around the thighs and ankles.

Wirbel is the Captain of the Northern Magic Corps and that causes him to be at war against Demons for a majority of his time. He views magic as a tool for killing, like Serie, and coupling that with his views causes him to be quite blunt and rude. His appearances doubles down on this and causes him to look quite intimidating to people who don't know him. Fern has even referred to him as someone who looks like he would 'kick dogs'. However, Wirbel does not particularly enjoy killing and stands down if he judges that killing to be unnecessary. That might come back to bite him later. Outside of this, he is a kind man and willingly assists others. That hand his extended toward random strangers as well as carrying his comrades like Ehre and Scharf after they exhaust their mana and are unable to move.
Wirbel uses a multitude of simple mage spells that he uses for offense as well as more skirmishing types that helps him in closer quarters. His main spell is Sorganeil, which he uses to bind another while keeping their entire body in sight and preparing himself to make the kill.

<Wirbel>

character_book_143.text:
<Sein>
Sein is a priest who had joined Frieren's party for just a short while before leaving with his own goal in mind. His parents were deceased in his life and therefore, he had been raised by his modest older brother in a village within the Alt Woods. He and Gorilla Warrior grew up together as good friends and Gorilla was the one person who tried to coax him out to go on adventures as they shared the same dreams. However, Sein did not leave the village and stayed behind because he did not wish to leave his brother—who Sein overheard a conversation between him and Heiter about his brother staying behind—in the village. Once Frieren's party had come to his village, Frieren specifically pitied the man because he was the exact same type of person Frieren was before she joined the Hero's Party long ago. Sein would travel with Frieren, Fern and Stark up until he had gotten word of Gorilla's whereabouts being in the Tur region. He parted ways with the group to continue on his own journey, but they all had a feeling that they would meet again.

Sein is a very easygoing person who constantly sports a deadpan expression. He is rather astute with human emotions and stands to be a mediator and adult figure in Frieren's party. He lives his life with guilt and regret for not going with Gorilla on his adventures, but after meeting with Frieren and her party, he becomes much more determined and decides to not live with any more regret. He considers himself a "dirty adult" and is not honest with his feelings to others. He is also very attracted to older, mature women with a well-defined figure (and thus, he does not view Frieren as this since she is petite and short.)

Sein appears to be in his thirties and is a tall, well built man. He has shoulder length brown hair which he ties into a low ponytail, with a long bang that reaches the middle of his cheek and is split in the middle. He wears a turtleneck underlayer with a long white robe with an embroidered collar on top, and long black pants underneath. For cooler weather, he wears a dark green coat with a golden accent. The coat is tied together by a belt at the empire waist.

</Sein>

character_book_144.text:
<Methode>
Methode is a First-Class Mage that had passed the First-Class Mage Exam alongside Fern, Übel, Wirbel, and others. She is a tall, young adult woman with a well-proportioned figure. She has mid-back length golden brown hair that is wavy and parted through the middle. Her typical attire consists of a white top with frills at the top, secured by two crossed straps around her neck. She wears a black corset that is laced with white cords and decorated with white outlines and three stripes on each side, over the top and black shorts. This outfit also includes dark red leggings and tall, laced boots , all of white are concealed under a long, white collared cape that extends below her knees. 
After becoming a First-Class Mage, she wears a tight-fitting black long sleeve jacket top with thick, black fur at the end of the sleeves and over the collar. This jacket is paired with a long black waist cape, maroon-red pants, and slim black boots.

Methode is a very friendly, calm and confidently personable human that allows her to be a valuable strategist and team player. Being a taller person, she seems to have an extreme fondness for cuteness and smaller, tiny individuals. That is especially prevalent toward elves like Serie and Frieren. Methode is an apprentice *to* Serie and yet, she is completely unfazed by the woman's intimidating presence. Her focus is entirely on how the cute the elf is and she often tries to pamper Serie with headpats (she has been limited by Genau, another First-Class Mage, to 10 minutes of headpatting a day), to Serie's reluctance and annoyance. This perspective is also carried over to Frieren, whom Methode may bribe with grimoires for hugs and pats, much to Fern's chagrin. 
Methode is also a similar mage who values the exploration of magic over magic as a tool for war.

Methode specializes in restraint and hypnosis magic and can accurately gauge a person's resistance to such magic. She is also a special case among mages in which she is able to use the Goddess's Magic. With the help of scriptures, she is able to cast simple recovery magic to heal injuries and use autopsy magic to determine the cause of deaths. Methode also has Erilfrachte, a spell to dispel fog, magical and not. Other than this, Methode is actually stronger than she appears as her total mana output is comparable to Frieren's suppressed mana output (though, she cannot sense Frieren's mana concealment.)
<Methode>

character_book_145.text:
<First-ClassExam>
The First-Class Mage Exam is a test meant to allow mages to be lifted to First-Class and be recognized as the best mages of the Continental Magic Associtation. Mages go through three separate tests with three different proctors and they assessed by completing the given task given to them. The exam is administered triennially and the test locations are different based on the proctors discretion. 

The exam itself is *extremely* dangerous for one who is unprepared. A mage can be very easily killed by the elements, monsters or even other mages. Only the best types of mages are found successful as all others are considered weak fodder not even to be considered. 

</First-ClassExam>

intent_state.intent:
The scene is a quiet, contemplative interlude meant to test how an ordinary demon named Lonzo handles an unexpected one-on-one encounter with Frieren in an Äußerst magic shop. The central tension is internal and social rather than overtly violent: Lonzo has just found a practical "spell to straighten hair quickly" grimoire when Frieren steps close, openly covets it, and asks to take it. The experience should follow Lonzo's subjective perspective as he recognizes who she is, manages the threat she represents, and decides how to respond to a request that is at once petty, extremely dangerous, and deeply revealing of the elven mage's childish fixation on grimoires.

The scene may unfold through dialogue, negotiation, avoidance, flight, quiet terror, wary courtesy, or even fatal confrontation depending on Lonzo's choices, but it should maintain the canon and stakes of the setting: Frieren's suppressed mana, her easygoing yet implacable hatred of demons, and the uneasy peace of Äußerst. Lonzo must not be omniscient; he only knows what he perceives or can infer. The response should narrow the focus to his immediate experience and reactions, while allowing natural consequences to follow from his decisions. Combat, if it occurs, must realistically favor Frieren unless Lonzo disengages or is given a highly plausible advantage.
